title: Representations Shape Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Theoretical Insights and Empirical Predictions
page_convention: One-based original-PDF pages; printed local pages coincide, 40 pages
summary: The Gaussian example's stated scaling does not imply the squared-rate isotropy condition needed for its advertised application of the main theorem; a separate finite inverse perturbation inequality is false but its inspected asymptotic use is recoverable.

problems.title: Gaussian example fails the claimed kernel-isotropy rate
problems.source_claim: Appendix C.2.1 claims the Gaussian family with d=omega(n²), sigma²=O(n), n=omega(k²) is (0,sigma²/n,sigma²/n)-decomposable; Example 4.2 invokes this for Corollary 4.3.

assumptions.distributions: y,z independent N(0,1); independent xi_w,xi_s~N(0,I_m/m); independent samples/splits

problems.hypothesis_verification: All explicit Gaussian specialization/Example4.2 premises hold: variances, independent coordinates, bounded label moment, d/n²→∞, 0<sigma²=o(n), beta=o(sigma²/n). The claimed decomposability conclusion is what fails; this is not a counterexample satisfying Assumption3.7 to Theorem3.8.
problems.suspect_step: Step after equation (34) assumes ordinary Gram concentration suffices for o(gamma²), with gamma=1/n.
problems.complete_check: A=(Xi^T Xi-I)/n. Conditional on xi1, offdiagonal first-column sum of squares equals ||xi1||² chi²_(n−1)/(mn²). Dividing its square root by gamma² gives sqrt[(chi²_m/m)(chi²_(n−1)/n)] for m=n³, converging to1. Therefore P(||A||op/gamma²>1/2)→1.
problems.result: Required o(gamma²) is false for an admissible Gaussian family.
counterevidence: A weaker o(gamma) requirement holds, but differs from printed Definition3.3 and changes inverse-error proof.
Final risk formulas and Theorem3.8 conditional on actual Assumption3.7 are not refuted.
Uses explicit Gaussian setting to avoid inconsistent sub-Gaussian parameter convention.
problems.impact: Invalid applicability derivation is directly used in central benign-overfitting Example4.2/Corollary4.3; does not establish empirical score harm or whole-paper failure.

correction.statement: For the specific independent Gaussian family with k=1 and sigma²=1, strengthen m/n³→∞.
correction.verification: Gaussian covariance bound gives ||A||op/gamma²≤4sqrt(n³/m)+4n²/m→0 with probability≥1−2exp(−n/2); other conditions remain valid.
correction.unverified: Full general sub-Gaussian theorem and original full parameter range.

problems.title: Finite inverse perturbation bound omits denominator
problems.source_claim: Lemma A.3 gives ||(A+Delta)^−1−A^−1||≤||A^−1||²||Delta|| for invertible A.
locations: Uses in Lemmas A.5–A.6, PDF p14
problems.hypothesis_verification: Both A and A+Delta invertible; scalar operator norm is absolute value.
problems.complete_check: Claimed RHS0.5; actual inverse difference |2−1|=1. Resolvent and Neumann-series bound add denominator1−||A^−1Delta||.
problems.result: Finite inequality false; corrected bound attained by scalar example.
counterevidence: In A.5 and A.6 under their genuine assumptions, ||A^−1Delta||=o(1), so denominator1−o(1) preserves the required o(1) rate.
problems.impact: Finite supporting inequality is incorrect; no independently established damage to inspected asymptotic conclusions from this item.

correction.statement: Require ||A^−1Delta||<1 and divide the stated RHS by1−||A^−1Delta||.
correction.verification: Analytic resolvent identity and geometric series bound; confirms A.5/A.6 rate preservation.

AppendixC.3 bounds cross covariance without showing it vanishes; intended dependence and subGaussian parameter conventions unresolved.
